# Adata Legend 840 – Low-priced PCIe Gen 4 SSD with Innogrit controller in review

 Simon Lüthje 18. August 2022 · 7 min.

...

The Legend 840 is, if we disregard Adata’s gaming brand Xtreme Performance Gear (XPG), the fastest SSD available from the manufacturer so far. The SSD achieves transfer rates of up to 5000 MB/s read and 4500 MB/s write and is thus in the midfield of PCIe Gen4x4 SSDs. Adata also wants to convince with a flat heat sink, which is also suitable for installation in Sony’s PlayStation 5, and a low price. On the technical side, the installed controller is a special feature. Adata uses the IG5220 from the manufacturer Innogrit, which was only founded in China in 2016, which clearly distinguishes the Legend 840 from the majority of available SSDs. We will clarify the performance of the IG5220 and how the SSD performs compared to the already tested models in the following test with the 1 TB model.

The SSD comes in the M.2 2280 form factor, and PCIe Gen 4 is used as the interface. The maximum sequential transfer rates are 5000 MB/s for reading and 4500 MB/s for writing. Besides the 1 TB model, which is available for our review, a smaller 512 GB model is also available. However, this only writes with up to 3400 MB/s, the read speed is also 5000 MB/s.

As mentioned at the beginning, the installed controller is a special feature of the SSD. While most of the competitors mainly use controllers from Phison or Silicon Motion, Adata uses the Innogrit IG5220, also known as the Rainier Q. The controller is not a standard one. With 7.5 x 11 mm, the controller is particularly small and also very cost- and energy-saving. Micron’s latest 3D NAND TLC (Micron B47R, 176 layers) is used as the memory. We have to do without a DRAM cache. The warranty period is 5 years or up to a write performance of 650 TB, which is very good for this price range.

...

Adata’s Legend 840 comes in a glossy box, the dimensions of which are reminiscent of those of a 2.5″ SSD. On the front, we find information about the PCIe 4.0 interface and the capacity next to a photo of the SSD including a gray heat sink. On the back, there is information about the speed and a QR code that leads to the technical specifications.

The M.2 SSD can always be seen with a heat sink in photos, but the SSD and heat sink are separated from each other in the box. If you want to use the included heatsink, you only have to stick it on the top of the SSD, a thermal pad is already attached. Due to the low height of the heat sink and the performance, the Legend 840 is not only suitable for use in the PC, but also for the PlayStation 5.
